item.title: IPA, Santos sign MoU to strengthen landowner companies and SMEs
item.description: The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has signed a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] with Santos Limited to design and deliver training programs aimed at boosting compliance and corporate governance for landowner companies and small businesses in resource areas. The agreement targets landowner company [landco] contractors and Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs] operating within Santos project-i
item.content:encoded:
The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has signed a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] with Santos Limited to design and deliver training programs aimed at boosting compliance and corporate governance for landowner companies and small businesses in resource areas.

The agreement targets landowner company [landco] contractors and Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs] operating within Santos project-impacted areas across Papua New Guinea.

IPA Managing Director Clarence Hoot and Santos Senior Vice President PNG Stakeholder Management Wayne Kasou officially signed the agreement.

Under the partnership, the IPA and Santos will develop capacity-building training to ensure local businesses operate transparently and comply with statutory requirements.

The initiative aligns with the IPA’s ongoing institutional reforms, which focus on modernizing the national company registry system and promoting sound corporate governance.

While landowner companies remain central business partners in Santos-operated petroleum and energy projects, many continue to face operational challenges surrounding board responsibilities and regulatory compliance.

Beyond compliance training, the partnership will also assist local landcos in exploring and developing new commercial opportunities within their project footprint.

The deal expands the IPA’s existing network of inter-agency and provincial partnerships aimed at decentralizing business support services.

The IPA maintains similar working MoUs with key state bodies including the Internal Revenue Commission, PNG Immigration and Citizenship Services, National Cultural Commission, National Gaming Control Board, and the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary Fraud Directorate, as well as provincial administrations to establish dedicated IPA Help Desks within provincial commerce divisions.

item.title: Peace to progress: Hayapuga communities rebuild church, schools after years of conflict
item.description: Communities in the Hayapuga local level government [LLG] of Tari-Pori district are turning the page on years of devastating tribal conflict, driving a rebuilding effort backed by new church infrastructure, education projects, and a local financial inclusion drive. Having stood as pillars of unity and peace restoration during times of unrest, churches in the area are now seeing direct support to re
item.content:encoded:
Communities in the Hayapuga local level government [LLG] of Tari-Pori district are turning the page on years of devastating tribal conflict, driving a rebuilding effort backed by new church infrastructure, education projects, and a local financial inclusion drive.

Having stood as pillars of unity and peace restoration during times of unrest, churches in the area are now seeing direct support to rebuild their foundations in Hela province.

Over the weekend, local community leader Tobby Maya Pajape visited the Yapiya Haronda ECPNG Church, pledging to personally purchase and deliver construction materials this month for a new church building and pastor’s house.

“I acknowledge the work of churches in the LLG who stood united during tribal conflicts to restore peace and unity,” Pajape said. “Because of their effort and the support of partners, the LLG is now beginning to witness real peace.”

To sustain this peace, Pajape has launched a targeted grassroots economic program aimed at empowering women and youth through financial structure.

He recently distributed Bank South Pacific [BSP] account opening forms to the Karai community to establish clan and group accounts, confirming that 10 new group accounts will be fully operational before the end of August.

“I want the community to get involved in Small to Medium Enterprise [SME] activities,” he urged residents. “First, clear the new site where Karai Primary School will be built. Work together in groups on agriculture, and support the church and school. In return, I will deposit funds into your accounts.”

He emphasized that establishing formal banking access gives local groups the structural foundation needed to manage SME initiatives and participate directly in local infrastructure projects.

With peace returning, local leaders are prioritizing education, one of the heaviest casualties of past tribal violence in Karai. Plans for Karai Primary School and the Karai Technical Vocational Education and Training [TVET] Centre were shelved for years due to instability, but full-scale restoration is now underway.

Hela Education Services has officially recognized the establishment of Karai Primary School, with student enrollments scheduled to open next year.

item.title: East Sepik PHA named amongst top 10 performing health authorities
item.description: East Sepik Provincial Health Authority [ESPHA] is among the top 10 performing Provincial Health Authorities in Papua New Guinea. This is according to the 2025 Sector Performance Annual Review [SPAR] of the National Department of Health [NDoH].
item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Provincial Health Authority [ESPHA] is among the top 10 performing Provincial Health Authorities in Papua New Guinea.

This is according to the 2025 Sector Performance Annual Review [SPAR] of the National Department of Health [NDoH].

East Sepik PHA was one of the least performing PHAs in the country ranking second last out of the 22 Provincial Health Authorities in 2022 to 2023.

However, due to improved reporting systems, it is ranked as the 9th among the 22 PHA's in the country in 2025.

In recent years, East Sepik PHA has made outstanding progress. This milestone achievement was revealed during the mid-term review workshop of East Sepik provincial health authority by health information manager Julius Wangama.

Wangama said the ranking demonstrates progress in strengthening health information systems.

However, he said the improvements are needed in reporting compliance, and timely submissions.

The presentation also revealed ongoing efforts to strengthen the National Health Information System including monthly reporting compliance, daily data entry, clinical reporting, and improved access to health information resources.

East Sepik PHA has applauded the leadership of chief executive officer Matthew Kaluvia, the senior executive management, board of governance, and its developing partners.

Health workers and staff across health facilities in East Sepik were also acknowledged for their collective contribution to the PHA’s performance.

item.title: Flood-prone crossings disrupt travel along Vanimo as heavy rain hits parts of West Sepik
item.description: Heavy rainfall in West Sepik has once again highlighted the ongoing challenges faced by commuters along the Vanimo West Coast Highway, with floodwaters covering several low-level culvert crossings and bringing traffic to a standstill. During periods of heavy rain, floodwaters quickly rise above the culvert crossings, making it impossible for most vehicles to pass safely.
item.content:encoded:
Heavy rainfall in West Sepik has once again highlighted the ongoing challenges faced by commuters along the Vanimo West Coast Highway, with floodwaters covering several low-level culvert crossings and bringing traffic to a standstill.

During periods of heavy rain, floodwaters quickly rise above the culvert crossings, making it impossible for most vehicles to pass safely.

Public Motor Vehicles [PMVs], private vehicles, government transport, and freight trucks are often forced to wait for hours until water levels subside.

The situation also affects school children, workers, patients travelling to health facilities, and families who rely on the highway for daily travel.

Residents say the problem has persisted for many years, despite repeated calls for temporary Bailey Bridges to be installed at flood-prone locations.

While commitments have been made in the past, communities continue to experience the same disruptions whenever heavy rain occurs.

The issue has gained renewed attention as the Vanimo–Daunda–Wutung Road is currently being upgraded under the Connect PNG Program and is now recognised as part of Papua New Guinea's National Highway network.

It also connects PNG to Indonesia, making it an important economic highway.

Local residents believe that installing temporary Bailey Bridges at critical flood crossings would provide a practical solution, ensuring safe and reliable access while permanent bridge infrastructure is planned and constructed.

They say reliable road access is essential for the movement of people, goods, emergency services, and economic activity.

Photos captured during the latest flooding show commuters waiting beside stranded vehicles, while some motorists cautiously attempt to drive through floodwaters in order to continue their journey.

As work on the Connect PNG project progresses, many residents are calling on the National Government and relevant authorities to prioritise temporary bridge solutions to improve year-round accessibility along one of West Sepik Province's most important transport corridors.

item.title: NAC and ODESH defend new Jackson’s Airport taxi system amid operator pushback
item.description: The National Airports Corporation [NAC] and transport provider ODESH Limited have clarified public discussions surrounding the selection of taxi operators at Jackson's International Airport, following pushback and online videos from unselected operators. NAC said the introduction of the new taxi arrangement was necessary to manage temporary space constraints caused by ongoing extension and refurbi
item.content:encoded:
The National Airports Corporation [NAC] and transport provider ODESH Limited have clarified public discussions surrounding the selection of taxi operators at Jackson's International Airport, following pushback and online videos from unselected operators.

NAC said the introduction of the new taxi arrangement was necessary to manage temporary space constraints caused by ongoing extension and refurbishment works at the Domestic Terminal, which significantly reduced parking and drop-off zones.

To maintain order, NAC publicly advertised invitations in The National and Post-Courier in 2024 and 2025, calling on qualified taxi operators to apply for the NAC Premium Taxi Service.

Contract awards went to three service providers meeting requirements, which included operating online/app-based booking platforms and maintaining modern fleet standards.

ODESH Limited, a 100 per cent Papua New Guinean-owned enterprise and dual SME award winner, refuted social media claims that the contract was awarded privately or through favoritism.

"ODESH submitted its application through the required process and was invited by NAC to attend a meeting alongside representatives from several taxi operators, including Comfort Taxi," ODESH stated in its press release.

"ODESH was selected through a publicly advertised and competitive process. The appointment was not made privately or without giving other qualified taxi operators an opportunity to apply."

ODESH added that all its vehicles are registered with the Road Traffic Authority [RTA] and Motor Vehicles Insurance Limited [MVIL], featuring valid taxi T-plates. On fare concerns raised by passengers, ODESH clarified that rates charged strictly follow the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission [ICCC] approved 2026 taxi fare structure.

Addressing initial rollout difficulties, NAC acknowledged operational challenges, including taxi shortages during peak flight arrival times. The corporation confirmed it has issued directives to contracted operators to scale up vehicle numbers.

However, NAC expressed concern over recent illegal disruptions at the airport terminal.

"NAC is concerned by recent incidents involving certain unauthorized taxi operators, including the intimidation of NAC staff, aggressive behavior, non-compliance with airport regulations, and damage to airport property," the corporation said in a media statement.

"Such conduct is unacceptable and will not be tolerated. The safety of passengers, airport users, and staff remains NAC’s highest priority."

NAC reassured local taxi operators that the procurement process is not permanently closed, encouraging operators willing to upgrade their services to contact NAC for operational and safety specifications to qualify for future opportunities.

item.title: SP Brewery backs Enga cultural show
item.description: South Pacific Brewery has backed the upcoming 2026 Enga Cultural Show with a sponsorship of K5,000 to assist the organizers with event preparations. The annual cultural event, which showcases the rich heritage and traditions of Enga Province, will take place from August 7-9 in Wabag town.
item.content:encoded:
South Pacific Brewery has backed the upcoming 2026 Enga Cultural Show with a sponsorship of K5,000 to assist the organizers with event preparations.

The annual cultural event, which showcases the rich heritage and traditions of Enga Province, will take place from August 7-9 in Wabag town.

SP Brewery Highlands Region External Affairs Manager Luke Beliga presented the cheque to members of the show committee in Port Moresby on Monday.

Beliga said the brewery was proud to partner with the event, stating its role in fostering local peace, social unity, and tourism growth in the province.

"We believe this event will continue to promote the culture of Enga, foster a safe and peaceful community, and boost tourism in the province," Beliga said.

"The show aligns closely with our purpose of fostering the joy of true togetherness, and we are grateful for the opportunity to help bring communities together while celebrating the diverse cultures that make Papua New Guinea unique."

Enga Cultural Show Committee chairlady Margaret Potane commended SP Brewery for its ongoing support and investment in community cultural preservation.

Potane said the show serves as an important platform for Engan people to celebrate their heritage, including traditional dances, chants, costumes, and unique rituals, while demonstrating resilience against modern influences.

"SP Brewery's sponsorship demonstrates a genuine commitment to preserving our cultural heritage, supporting our people, and strengthening the spirit of unity and togetherness that this show represents," Potane said.

The contribution is part of SP Brewery’s ongoing corporate social responsibility efforts to support community initiatives and preserve local customs across the country.

item.title: New Ireland traditional leaders petition provincial government over administrative vacuum
item.description: Traditional leaders representing communities across New Ireland Province have petitioned the Provincial Government and Administration, demanding urgent action over the prolonged vacancy in the office of the Provincial Administrator. The chiefs gathered outside the Provincial Administration this Tuesday morning, where they staged a peaceful customary protest by placing a taboo marker - a tanget pla
item.content:encoded:
Traditional leaders representing communities across New Ireland Province have petitioned the Provincial Government and Administration, demanding urgent action over the prolonged vacancy in the office of the Provincial Administrator.

The chiefs gathered outside the Provincial Administration this Tuesday morning, where they staged a peaceful customary protest by placing a taboo marker - a tanget plant at the entrance to the administration building.

The symbolic act reflected their call for an acting Provincial Administrator to be appointed while the province awaits the appointment of a substantive office holder.

Speaking on behalf of the communities, and chiefs concerned, Makis said people have endured months of disruptions to government services since the Provincial Administrator resigned in June.

They claimed the absence of leadership has negatively affected service delivery across the province.

In the afternoon, the group of chiefs returned with three petition papers, to present it to the government and administration, and at the same time, removed the tanget.

At approximately 3pm, provincial government and administration officials formally received the petition and assured the leaders that it would be tabled at the next Provincial Executive Council meeting before an official response is provided.

The provincial administration and government each contributed K500 cash and one mis each, in recognition of their plight and acknowledgment for removing the taboo from the administration office.

The meeting concluded with both parties reaching an understanding, with the traditional leaders agreeing to await the provincial government's official response while maintaining their call for urgent action to restore effective leadership and improve services for the people of New Ireland.

item.title: Turi slams lawyers misleading settlers
item.description: Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi has condemned lawyers representing illegal settlers, accusing them of knowingly pursuing unwinnable cases and misleading clients into believing they have a chance of success. He said most of the disputed land is either state owned or held by private companies, yet settlers continue to occupy it while claiming legitimacy.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Commissioner of Police and NCD Central Commander Benjamin Turi has condemned lawyers representing illegal settlers, accusing them of knowingly pursuing unwinnable cases and misleading clients into believing they have a chance of success.

He said most of the disputed land is either state owned or held by private companies, yet settlers continue to occupy it while claiming legitimacy.

Turi accused certain lawyers of exploiting this ignorance for financial gain, dragging cases through the courts despite knowing they will fail.

“It is the lawyer’s responsibility to be honest and inform their clients that the land does not belong to them. Why fool poor settlers until they run out of money and end up homeless?” ACP Turi said.

He said such actions waste police resources, frustrate the courts, and prolong disputes that should have been resolved from the start.

Turi also referenced the recent directive from the National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] instructing squatters to vacate NBC land, stressing that the land belongs to NBC and illegal occupants have no legal standing.

“My advice to the people illegally occupying NBC land is to simply move out. Don’t try to challenge this in court, you will be fooled like other settlers misled by certain lawyers. The land belongs to NBC, and police will move in to evict people forcefully once the court order is served,” he said.

item.title: Daki breaks silence on K200m SME allegations, welcomes audit
item.description: Tambul-Nebilyer MP and former Commerce and Industry Minister Win Bakri Daki has broken his silence on allegations surrounding the government's K200 million Small to Medium Enterprise [SME] stimulus policy, welcoming an audit and insisting it will clear his name.
